Exercise A

A Festival That Travelled

Read the text, then choose the correct answer to each question.

Before you read — optional, not marked
You can leave this empty. It does not count towards your score.
Reading text

Halloween began as part of old seasonal traditions in Ireland and Britain. Samhain marked the start of winter in the traditional Irish calendar. People carved turnips into frightening lanterns and wore disguises. They also played games and visited neighbours for food and entertainment.

In the nineteenth century, Irish and Scottish immigrants took Halloween customs to North America. Pumpkins were larger and softer than turnips, so they were easier to carve. The pumpkin lantern became the jack-o'-lantern we know today.

Modern Halloween is a mixture of old and new traditions. Children dress in costumes, neighbours decorate their porches, and families tell spooky stories. In many places, trick-or-treating is also a social event: people meet, talk and share treats. A frightening festival can therefore bring a community together.

Exercise D

Writing: The Lantern in the Window

Your school newspaper needs a Halloween story. Write 70–90 words to entertain younger readers and give your story a surprising ending.

Plan your story

Beginning: On a dark Halloween evening, you saw a lantern in an empty house.

Middle: Describe two strange things that happened and how you felt.

Ending: Explain the lantern—or surprise the reader.
